At 11¢ you're in good shape — the Airsquitter is an ADS-B receiver, not a hashing miner, so it sips power rather than pulling hundreds of watts. It's $985.83, and it earns by feeding aircraft data from your roof or window.

Is this your first DePIN box, or are you adding to something you already run?
this is my first want to learn about how this works

Here's the short of it. The red sensor box sits indoors on ethernet or WiFi; the 1090 MHz antenna goes on a roof mast or in the attic with a clear view of sky. It picks up ADS-B/Mode-S signals from aircraft up to 250 nautical miles out and feeds them to the 4DSKY network, and you get credited for the coverage you provide.

Honest part: 4DSKY is still on testnet — you earn $4DSKY points, no token and no launch date yet.

Where would the antenna go, roof or attic?

Attic is fine — it's the common install. Just know a foil-backed or metal roof will cut your range a lot; a mast outside always reaches further.

The kit comes with the antenna, mast clamps, antenna and ethernet cables, universal plug, plus 3 months of Moken DePIN Tracker Pro.

Which country are you in? The variant is region-matched, and that sets the price.
USA and do you need a depin accont after the 3 months?

No. Moken is an optional dashboard for watching your DePIN gear — the Airsquitter keeps feeding 4DSKY and earning points whether you renew or not. After three months you just decide if the Pro plan is worth it to you.

For the US it's the Standard Antenna (USA) variant at $985.83, and it's live right now. Want me to build the cart?
what can I use 4dsky points on?

Nothing yet, honestly. They're testnet credit for the coverage you provide — there's no token, no redemption and no announced launch date, so I can't promise they convert to anything.

What's actually moving: the founder says 4DSKY has paying customers, runs on Hedera, and will start paying operators small USDC rewards. Early operators hold the coverage map when that starts.

Buy it for the hardware and the early position, not a payout.
are their any USA company interest ?

Straight answer: I don't know who 4DSKY's paying customers are — the founder said they have them, but no names have been published, and I won't guess at US ones.

What I can say is the sensor is Jetvision hardware, the same aviation-grade kit FlightRadar24, FlightAware and aerospace and defence firms use.

I'll put the customer question to Georges. What email should the answer go to?
ok another question is can I login and see the data it gets and sends ?

Yes. The A. runs its own local web interface on your network — you point a browser at the box and see live aircraft, message rates and signal stats, so you can tell right away how well the attic antenna is doing. On top of that there's the 4DSKY side for your points, and Moken Pro for the at-a-glance view.

Still happy to get Georges that customer question — what email should it go to?
not right now but does it also tell you like the tail number of the planes that fly over and things like flight tracker 24 ?

Yes, that's exactly the data. Each aircraft broadcasts its hex ID, callsign/flight number, altitude, speed and position, and you see it live on your own box. The tail number comes from looking that hex up in a registry database — which is what FlightRadar24 does with feeds like yours. So you're running the same source they do.

Ready for me to build that cart?

context.pop: What do you pay for power? I'll run the Airsquitter numbers for where you live.
